notes: Dadiwan culture of the Wei River valley, the first farmers of eastern Gansu and Shaanxi; the page dates it 'c. 5800-5400 BCE' (and 'c. 7900-7200 BP' in a BP sequence) and says its ceramics are a 'thin-walled, cord-marked ceramic tradition' that is 'sometimes referred to as Laoguantai'; the Laoguantai culture's own Wikipedia page could not be loaded (URL_NOT_FOUND), so the two are one dossier here. Extent: 'located mainly in eastern Gansu and Shaanxi provinces', type site in Qin'an County on the Qingshui, 'a tributary of the Wei River'; no site count and no area. The Tianshui disc (100 km) plus Guanzhong is drawn, confidence 2. The culture 'shares pottery, architecture, and economic features with the Cishan and Peiligang cultures to the east'. Succession: 'The Yangshao follows Dadiwan in the local sequence' (the page dates the Yangshao there to 6800-4900 BP; the Yangshao page says c. 5000 BC), so the Wei valley is nobody's land 5399..5001 here. The Yangshao dossier gains the Gansu disc in 5000 from nobody. No Cliopatria shape, no area figure.
